articles.title: NVIDIA Kumo: Foundation Models for Tabular Data (with Stanford Prof. Jure Leskovec)
articles.description:
#NVIDIAKumo #TabularFoundationModels #GraphNeuralNetworks

In Episode #1047, Jure Leskovec (Professor of Computer Science at Stanford and co-founder of Kumo AI, now part of NVIDIA) joins  @JonKrohnLearns to explain how a foundation model that has never seen real data can beat hand-built models on enterprise tables. These models need no feature engineering and no training. Jure pioneered graph neural networks, and since NVIDIA acquired Kumo, his team has released the full Kumo family as open weights under a license that allows commercial use. In this episode, Jure breaks down the four Kumo models for tabular, relational, forecasting and anomaly-detection tasks, explains how they are pre-trained on synthetic data, describes how Biomni came to be used by more than 10,000 scientists within weeks and lays out why he believes human judgment has never been more valuable.

In this episode you will learn:
• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:06:18) How Kumo Tabular makes predictions without any training
• (00:16:19) Pre-training tabular models on purely synthetic data
• (00:27:27) Kumo Relational and treating a database as a graph
• (00:54:28) Why human judgment is becoming more valuable

articles.title: Bosch Rexroth: What's your secret sauce?
articles.description: We discuss what happens when AI moves from answering questions to configuring automation, writing PLC code, and building machine visualizations. Bosch Rexroth’s Sebastian Krauskopf explains how Agent iXi uses domain knowledge, tools, and human approval to support engineering while keeping people in control. We also look at the bigger shifts around manufacturing AI, MES, acquisitions, and the changing value of engineering skills. The question is not just what agents can do, but how automation systems can become reliable and ready for them.
